title: Tenant-aware dashboard rollout plan and oncall quickcards
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working plan for rolling out a new tenant-aware dashboard surface and a compact set of oncall quickcards. The dashboard is intended to surface tenant-weighted SLIs, cold-cache hotspots, and per-route cost attribution so oncall can quickly decide whether an alert is tenant-specific, model-related, or platform-wide.

Goals (high level):
- Make it trivial for a single operator to assess an incident in <= 5 minutes using the dashboard + one trace.
- Reduce false-positive alerts by adding tenant-weight weighting and dynamic alert thresholds (burst-aware).
- Keep query-cost impact under a 15% increase vs current dashboards by staging probe cadence and rollup windows.
- Provide a minimal set of compact quickcards (text + 3 links) for common investigation paths.

Non-goals:
- Not a full rework of all observability panels. Focused set: latency SLOs, kv-cache warmth, model-fanout counts, per-tenant cost-run rates.

Key definitions (working):
- SLI: user-visible first-token latency (time_to_first_token_ms) — measured server-side at ingress edge, excludes client RTT. Rolling 1m/5m/1h.
- SLI: tail-token-latency-p99 (token_emit_latency_ms_p99) — backend emission latency per token for chat/generate endpoints.
- Metric: kv_cache_hit_rate_tenant — fraction of requests that hit read-only KV cache per-tenant (1m window).
- Metric: cold_start_rate_tenant — fraction of requests that required a cold model load or cold KV fill (30s TTL) per-tenant.
- Feature flag: tenant-weighted-alerting — when on, alerts use tenant priority multiplier to adjust thresholds.

Dashboard surface (panels to include):
1) Tenant-weighted SLO overview (top row)
   - Rows: tenant name | effective SLI (1m median) | SLI trend 1h | SLO burn rate 24h | cost delta 24h
   - Note: effective SLI = baseline SLI adjusted by tenant weight factor (configurable list). Weighting helps prioritize high-value tenants in paging thresholds.

2) Latency histogram + quantile-slicing
   - Interactive quantile slicer: choose tenant(s), route(s), model variant(s). Helpful to compare p50/p95/p99 across tenants.

3) KV cache warmth map
   - Per-tenant KV warmth index (0-100). Attach probe: synthetic-prefix-warm-check that fires 1m per 5m (see probe schedule below).

4) Model fanout and fallback rate
   - Track model version fanout counts, fallback to smaller variants, fallback success rate, and per-tenant fallback attribution.

5) Cost attribution panel (compact)
   - Daily token units consumed by tenant, per-route breakdown, amortized GPU-time estimate. Accept approximate numbers to avoid heavy queries.

6) Investigation quick-strip (compact)
   - Buttons/links to: single trace for a sample request, prompt replay view, tenant recent error log, recent rollouts touching model or runtime config.

Trace and annotation conventions (proposal):
- session_id first-class: all requests must carry session_id (or request_id) and tenant_id. Trace should anchor on session_id when present.
- Annotation keys: kvcache.hit=true/false, model.variant=, route.name=, rollout.id=, tenant.priority=low|normal|high.
- Sampling: adaptive sampling that ensures 1 trace/min per-tenant when tenant requests > 1r/s, otherwise keep 1 trace/10m baseline. Priority tenants get increased trace budget.

Alerting philosophy and gating rules:
- Tiered alerts: 
  - Tier 1 (pager): sustained tenant-weighted SLO violation > 10m AND absolute p99 > 800ms OR cold_start_rate_tenant > 5% AND tenant.priority=high.
  - Tier 2 (slack): transient burn > 5 for 5m or cost spike > 3x expected for > 10m.
- Auto-mitigation allowed: if fallback rate > 30% and fallback success rate > 95%, do not page; instead open a P1 internal ticket.

Probe schedule and query-cost plan (to control dashboard cost):
- Synthetic probes: prefix-warm-check per-region, per-tenant sampling:
  - Canary tenants (10 tenants): probe every 60s
  - High-priority tenants (top 50 by ARR): probe every 2m
  - All other tenants: rotating probe, one tenant per 5m slot (spreads cost across tenants).
- Aggregation windows: store 1m resolution for 7d, 5m for 30d, 1h beyond. This reduces dashboard query cost for weekly views.
- Query budget target: new panels should add <15% query cost to the observability dashboard cluster. We'll measure via query-cost dashboard.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (now): narrow internal alpha with dev+SRE tenants only. Validate metrics, sampling, and labels.
- Phase 1 (rolling canary, 10 tenants): enable tenant-weighted alerts in quiet hours. Monitor false positives for 48h.
- Phase 2 (expanded, 50 tenants): add cost attribution panel; enable limited tracing budget for these tenants.
- Phase 3 (GA): open to all tenants; enable UI controls for operator to toggle tenant weight and probe cadence.

Acceptance criteria for promotion between phases:
- No more than 1 noisy alert per 24h attributable to mislabeling or sampling changes.
- Query cost delta below 15% after aggregation tuning.
- Oncall triage median time to meaningful trace <= 5 minutes (measured on the investigation-runbook dashboard).

Oncall quickcards (compact operator steps):
- Quickcard A: High p99 page (tenant-weighted)
  1) Check tenant-weighted SLO overview (top row) -> is single tenant flagged or many?
  2) Open the quantile slicer for that tenant and route. If p95 is fine and p99 high, suspect tail/fanout.
  3) Open one trace (investigation quick-strip) anchored by session_id. Look for kvcache.hit=false or model.load events.
  4) If cold_start events present, check recent rollouts (link) and cold_start_rate_tenant in the last 30m.
  5) If it's an infra spike (all tenants), escalate to runtime-oncall. If single tenant and high priority, call CS lead.

- Quickcard B: Cost spike alert
  1) Open cost attribution panel -> isolate top 3 routes and top model variants.
  2) Check recent rollout.id annotations in traces. If rollout present, rollback or open immediate investigation.
  3) If no rollout, apply temporary rate-limit or advise customer-specific quota while continued investigation occurs.

- Quickcard C: Error surge / high 5xx
  1) Check per-tenant error panel, filter to route.
  2) Open sample trace; look for model.throw or runtime OOM.
  3) If OOM or GPU resource contention flagged, enable fallback by increasing fallback ratio in routing policy.

Ownership and next steps:
- Owner: Ava Nguyen (eng-observability) – coordinate with SRE and solutions engineering.
- Dev tasks: add tenant.priority tag to runtime (ENG-OBS-PR-42), implement probe scheduler (ENG-OBS-PR-44).
- SRE tasks: define sampling knobs and update trace retention policy.
- Product: confirm tenant-weight list and priority rubric for first 50 tenants.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we reconcile tenant weight with multi-tenant requests (shared API keys)? Need a mapping heuristic — TODO Diego.
- Are we comfortable with the per-tenant probe rotation frequency for low-volume tenants? Check with cost team.
- Investigate whether we can compute approximate cost attribution offline to reduce dashboard load.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep panels compact; aim for one-screen triage. Use links instead of heavy aggregations where possible.
- During Phase 1 expect a lot of label fixes; make it easy to flip sampling/weighting flags.

End of draft.

Comments welcome — leave inline comments or ping in #observability when making changes.
